normalized.description: ESA is encouraging the implementation of a circular economy' in space that ensures long-term orbital sustainability through in-orbit servicing. Several activities comprise the circular economy in space, namely on-orbit assembly, on-orbit manufacturing, and on-orbit recycling, all supported by technologies for on-orbit servicing, rendezvous, and close-proximity operations. These technologies will allow us to treat orbital space as a finite resource, re-use space assets, and minimize the waste associated with building and disposing of spacecraft.ESA concluded a studies campaign in early 2025, which supported four pre-Phase A industrial feasibility studies looking at on-orbit refurbishment, manufacturing, and recycling in Earth orbit. From these studies, two concepts have been selected as winners of the campaign and their concepts have been consolidated together with ESA experts by performing Concurrent Design studies at ESA ESTEC Concurrent Design Facility. As outcome of this work, ESA has identified on-orbit refurbishment as its primary near-term goal for the next generation of circular economy activities through in-orbit servicing capabilities. The scope of the proposed work will be to mature the on-orbit refurbishment concept with a Phase A study focusing on the design of an in-orbit demonstration missions and the identification of the critical technologies to be developed in the next coming years.The procurement will be open competition to all industrial entities, ensuring an opencompetitive approach preparing further steps. Parallel contracts may be placed in case of competitive complementary proposals.
